question: By selling an article for ₹4,824 , a man gains 20%. What will be his profit percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer) if he sells it for ₹6,000?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By unitary method, if selling price ₹4,824 corresponds to 120% of Cost Price.

Then, the percentage value for ₹6,000 = (120 ÷ 4824) × 6000

⇒ Percentage value = 60000 ÷ 402 = 149.25%

New Profit % = 149.25% − 100% = 49.25% ≈ 49%

**∴ The correct answer is 49%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹4,824

Initial Profit Percentage = 20%

New Selling Price (SP₂) = ₹6,000

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit %)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (4824 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP = 482400 ÷ 120 = ₹4,020

⇒ New Profit = New SP − CP = 6000 − 4020 = ₹1,980

⇒ New Profit % = (1980 ÷ 4020) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (198 ÷ 402) × 100 = (33 ÷ 67) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = 3300 ÷ 67 ≈ 49.25%

⇒ Rounding to nearest integer, New Profit % ≈ 49%

**∴ The correct answer is 49%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base Reference for Profit & Loss

Cost Price (CP) is always considered the base value (100%) for calculating profit or loss percentages unless specified otherwise.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ True Weight − Error) × 100.
